items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because the current implementation of structure_load in ActiveRecord::Tasks::SQLiteDatabaseTasks uses a backtick-executed shell command to invoke sqlite3.
This approach directly interpolates supplied values (such as the database name) into the command string, which could allow command injection if a maliciously crafted database path is used.

By switching to Kernel.system with properly separated arguments, we prevent unescaped shell interpretation and ensure the command is executed safely.

No functional behavior changes are expected under normal conditions.

From H1 report @jhawthorn @matthewd

items.content_html:
The existing documentation implied that the "hard to guess" URLs active storage generates provides some sort of access control. This is not the case. Rather, as they rely on ActiveRecord::SignedId, they're tamper proof and don't expose the underlying id.

The security risk of using these URLs isn't that someone will guess them. Rather, it is if the URLs are ever leaked, the files will be exposed.

This happened to us via Cloudflare's crawler hints feature.

But there is a myriad of other ways it could happen. E.g. anyone with access to the request log has access to them, they might be exposed via certain analytics tools, even if a user has access to the app revoked they'll still have access to any files, etc.

Because of this, whenever any access control is needed, proxy and redirect mode should not be used.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Postgresql and Mysql have different behaviors regarding the sorting order of NULL.

For example:

z = Book.create!(name: "Zulu", author: authors(:david))
y = Book.create!(name: "Yankee", author: authors(:mary))
x = Book.create!(name: "X-Ray", author: authors(:david))
n = Book.create!(name: nil, author: authors(:bob))

# In postgreSQL
Book.order(name: :asc) # => [ x, y, z, n ]
# In MySQL/SQLite3
Book.order(name: :asc) # => [ n, x, y, z ]

Allowing asc_nulls_first and desc_nulls_last enables more control on sorting.

Detail

Usage:

Book.order(name: :asc_nulls_first)
Book.order(name: :ASC_NULLS_FIRST)
Book.order(name: "asc_nulls_first")
Book.order(Book.arel_table["name"].asc_nulls_first)
Book.order(books: { name: :asc_nulls_first })

items.content_html:
The s3_service exposes it's respective client and bucket attributes publicly. I think this makes sense in the context of active storage, as it allows users to rely on the same adapter & configs that the framework is using for Activestorage without having to duplicate your own client and ensure it matches the original, which can be modified at runtime, in order to perform operations outside of the scope of ActiveStorage.

This commit serves to make the same true of the gcs_service, which currently defined it's respective client & bucket as private method definitions.

I did a bit of git snooping and didn't see any mention of this being an intentional decision when first released.

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
items.title: Refactor gcs_service public interface to bring more in line with s3_service

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #55845

Routes with optional segments currently treat nil values correctly (omitting them from the path), but empty strings ('') are not treated the same way. This creates malformed URLs with double slashes and incorrect query parameters.

This is particularly problematic because form parameters often come through as empty strings rather than nil, leading to inconsistent and unexpected behaviour.

Example:

# Route defined as:
get '(/a/:a_id)(/b/:b_id)(/c/:c_id)', to: 'test#index', as: :optional_segments

# With nil (works correctly):
optional_segments_path(a_id: nil, b_id: 2, c_id: 3)  # => "/b/2/c/3"

# With empty string (broken):
optional_segments_path(a_id: '', b_id: 2, c_id: 3)   # => "/a//b/2/c/3"

Detail

This PR normalizes blank values to nil for route parameters before path generation in ActionDispatch::Journey::Formatter#generate. The fix:

  1. Adds a small loop that checks each route parameter for blank values and converts them to nil
  2. Only affects actual route parameters (defined in the route pattern) - non-route parameters can still have blank values
  3. Leverages all existing nil-handling logic

The normalization happens before extract_parameterized_parts is called, which prevents blank route parameters from becoming query parameters like ?a_id=.

Additional information

Why normalize to nil instead of other approaches:

  • All existing logic already handles nil correctly (drop_while checks, compact!, query param filtering)
  • Minimal change - no modifications to existing logic needed
  • Preserves ability for non-route params to have blank values

Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because of security vulnerability detailed in #55843. The default rails authentication generator produces code that could allow a targeted man-in-the-middle attack to take place.

Detail

This Pull Request changes the options passed when creating the session cookie.
Simply adding the secure: true option stops the cookie being sent over insecure connections.

Additional information

  • Stack overflow post explaining vulnerability
  • Rails Docs which show that the secure option defaults to false

items.content_html:
If you're using Active Storage, but don't have image_processing gem installed, because the [default analyzers]1 includes Vips and ImageMagick analyzers, you would see the following error:

[ActiveJob] Enqueued ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob ...
[ActiveJob] [ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob] Performing ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob ...
[ActiveJob] [ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob] [0efa0f81-23e0-4a09-9fb2-55ecb484c10a] Error performing ActiveStorage::AnalyzeJob: NameError (uninitialized constant Vips):

Previously, this would rescue LoadError because the gems were required lazily.2

def read_image
  begin
    require "ruby-vips"
  rescue LoadError
    logger.info "Skipping image analysis because the ruby-vips gem isn't installed"
    return {}
  end

  # ...

Thanks to @claudiob for [reporting]3 and @Earlopain for all your help with this issue!

Footnotes

  1. https://guides.rubyonrails.org/configuring.html#config-active-storage-analyzers ↩

  2. https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/ab8e833991e493f57f03c10ee2a8a7fda218faae/activestorage/lib/active_storage/analyzer/image_analyzer/vips.rb#L13-L18 ↩

  3. https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/55697#issuecomment-3364212327 ↩
items.title: Skip analyze job if ruby-vips or mini_magick gem are missing

Motivation / Background

The "Delegated Types" section in the Association Basics guide contained the phrase:

"In order to apply this to our example above, we need to regenerate our models."

This was confusing because the preceding example is about STI and vehicles, which is unrelated to delegated types. As a result, readers could not easily understand what "example above" referred to.

This Pull Request clarifies the documentation so that the Delegated Types section is self-contained and easier to follow.

Fixes #55815

Detail

This Pull Request changes the documentation in guides/source/association_basics.md by:

  • Adding a NOTE clarifying that Delegated Types examples are independent from the STI “Vehicle” example.
  • Rewording the introduction in 6.2 Generating Models to explicitly reference the Entry, Message, and Comment models instead of “example above.”

No code changes were made. Only documentation was updated.

Additional information

  • Improves clarity for newcomers learning Delegated Types.
  • Ensures the section stands alone without relying on unrelated STI examples.
